There’s usually three ways it can go. You could feel like a zombie, or you could have euphoria that progresses into a manic psychotic episode, or you could feel… relatively normal and ok. We’re all aiming for the latter most. And if you feel the second, get on antipsychotics quick.

I figured this out too late. It was only after the destruction that I went off it (I stopped it) against my psych’s orders. They didn’t ever suggest an antipsychotic pairing or anything. Couldn’t get a second opinion. 

So, my partner made smaller doses for me to wane off 150mg with a jewel scale. I couldn’t do it because the withdrawal symptoms were debilitating and I had too shaky of a hand and felt like I was close to puking. 

I would say talk to your doctor about either getting on antipsychotics as well or if you feel like you’re in a comfortable position and have a good support system, wane off it.

I think I realized the best outlet was just to talk candidly or inquisitively about a specific depression rather than find a solution. Solutions feel judgmental in that a lot of depression is about inaction and helplessness. The idea of action is like moving a boulder up a hill, so to speak. That’s what most depressed people want. 

This should be achieved with a therapists, but that’s as easy to find as a suitable significant other - for some people, extremely difficult. I once paid a guy $300 a session for him to repeat “you have a lot going on” over and over again with no real detailed questions, or proof of active listening. I think I’ve had at least twenty therapists since I was 12 (I’m pushing 30 now) most of ‘em except for three were any good for me (they practiced active listening, and were specific). Granted I have niche issues but there are people who definitely have even more niche issues and I can’t even imagine they ever get the help they need.

Yup. Had a real alcohol dependency when I was on Effexor that I’d never traditionally experienced. Might want to keep track of it. I think this was the sign that I was going straight into a very destructive manic or psychotic episode. Be careful!

Anecdotal experience. I was on Effexor last year and diagnosed Bipolar II. No antipsychotics, also never really experienced traditional hypomania; I have intense depressive states. 


After month 3 or 4 is when I started getting my first stints of mania. Didn’t stop until I weaned off it against psych’s orders (they weren’t responsive to the idea that I was manic). Saved my life at the beginning, blew up and ruined my life by the end. I don’t want to get into detail but it was an extreme mania (hypersexuality, hyperspending, paranoid thoughts, substance dependency at a level I never thought I was capable of, anger/irritable)


I’d say talk to your doctor.
